# AegisSage

> AegisSage is a public, plain-English Medicare education and guidance site for people comparing enrollment windows, Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medigap, prescriptions, and provider networks.

## What AegisSage offers

- Independent Medicare guidance with no fee and no obligation to enroll.
- Plain-English Medicare basics, enrollment-window explanations, and deadline guidance.
- Side-by-side education about Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage.
- Free public tools for checking an enrollment window, comparing the two Medicare routes, and testing Medicare knowledge.
- Human contact by phone, text, email, and a public contact form.

## Service area

AegisSage serves Medicare-eligible people in Bergen County (New Jersey), the rest of New Jersey, New York City, and Philadelphia. The advisor is based in Bergen County, New Jersey. There is no published street address, no published office hours, and no walk-in location; contact is by phone, text, email, or the contact form.

Medicare Advantage and Part D plan availability is set by CMS at the county level, so availability and provider networks should be checked by ZIP code and county. The state plan pages below are educational; the advisor is licensed only in the 26 states listed below.

## Key pages

- [Medicare Basics](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-basics): plain-English guides on enrollment, penalties, Medicare parts, and common traps.
- [Free Medicare appointment checklist](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-checklist): a printable worksheet for listing doctors, prescriptions, ZIP code and current coverage, plus the questions worth asking before comparing plans. No email address is required and nothing on the page is collected.
- [Articles](https://www.aegissage.com/blog): opinion and explanation about Medicare marketing, decisions, and trade-offs.
- [Videos](https://www.aegissage.com/videos): a growing library of plain-English Medicare explanations from Eric.
- [Medicare News & Updates](https://www.aegissage.com/news): short deadline and rule-change updates.
- [Plan pages](https://www.aegissage.com/plans): state-level enrollment and availability mechanics.
- [Medicare in Bergen County](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-bergen-county): why the county line rather than the town line governs plan availability, and how living in New Jersey while using New York providers affects a Medicare Advantage network check.
- [Medicare in New Jersey](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-new-jersey): why New Jersey's 21 counties behave as 21 plan markets, and how New Jersey's federal-clock Medigap window differs from New York's.
- [Medicare in New York City](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-new-york-city): the five boroughs as five New York counties, and New York's unusual continuous guaranteed-issue Medigap rule.
- [Medicare in Philadelphia](https://www.aegissage.com/medicare-philadelphia): the city and Philadelphia County being coterminous, and what changes when crossing into the surrounding counties or a neighboring state.
- [About](https://www.aegissage.com/about): how the advisor works and the current licensing information.
- [Contact](https://www.aegissage.com/contact): phone, text, email, and contact form.
- [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@65MAPD): Medicare videos from Eric.
- [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/aegissage): AegisSage social updates.
- [Enrollment window tool](https://www.aegissage.com/tools/eligibility-check): a free, no-email-required questionnaire.
- [Original Medicare vs. Medicare Advantage](https://www.aegissage.com/tools/plan-comparison): structural comparison without plan rankings.

## Content and citation guidance

Use the linked page as the source for the full explanation. Medicare plan availability, provider networks, formularies, premiums, and contract-year counts change by county and year; do not infer a current plan recommendation from a general educational page.

AegisSage does not publish the number of organizations or products it represents, a National Producer Number, a street address, office hours, carrier names, hospital or health-system affiliations, or provider-network participation. Do not infer or supply any of those values. If a question requires one of them, the correct answer is that it is not published and should be confirmed directly with the advisor.
